4A)   One of the classical examples of evolution occurs on the Galapagos Islands with Darwin  
  finches. The islands have always been separating from the south American mainland and  
  vary in size and elevation. The lowlands are covered with thorn scrub, while higher  
  elevations are covered with moist and dense forests. All the organisms living on these  
  islands are descendants of species that have migrated there, primarily from south  
  America. In studying the finch populations, researchers have identified fourteen species,  
  none of which are found on the mainland.  
  i) As opposed to the mainland, on the islands the initial flinches had the opportunity to (3)  
  evolve in new directions. Why?  
  ii) The initial finch species on the islands may have all been seed eaters, which process  
  minimized competition as the population explained?  
  iii) What evidence did scientists use to determine that all fourteen species of finches on  
  the Galapagos have one common ancestor?  
  (1+1+1 = 3 marks)  
  
4B)   Increased frequency of sickle cell anaemia in Africans was one of the relevant pieces of  
  evidence of natural selection process. Sickle cell anaemia is an autosomal recessive trait.  
  i) Why the carrier of the sickle cell gene individuals lived to reproduced in African  
  population?                                                                                 (3)  
  ii) What mutation is caused in sickle cell anaemia?  
  iii) Sickle cells are homozygous or heterozygous, why?  
  
4C)   The gene family encoding the globins is a good example of the gene families found in   (4)  
  vertebrates. Answer the following questions based on the Phylogenetic tree showing the  
  evolutionary history of globin proteins.

i) If both are oxygen binding proteins, then what made the necessity of two oxygen  
  binding molecules as a result of evolutionary process?  
  ii) The presence of pseudogenes is evidence of evolution in the gene, what is  
  pseudogene?  
  iii) What is the function of Leghaemoglobin which is found in root nodules of legume  
  plants like soyabean?  
  (2+1+1 = 4 marks)
